summary: Voltline Health: inflight-queue exhaustion causing stream silence and session evictions during peak batch window
description:
Issue summary:
During Voltline Health's morning batch window (08:30–09:15 local), a sudden surge in concurrent ephemeral sessions exhausted per-customer inflight queues on several serving nodes, causing streaming responses to drop to silence mid-generation and resulting in session evictions for ~18% of requests.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: truncated or silent streaming completions and connection resets for conversational endpoints used by Voltline's triage assistant.
- Business: enterprise customer reported degraded UX impacting live triage flows; on-call sales/CS escalation opened.
- Metrics: 5xx rate for the customer's tenant peaked at 6.8% for 25 minutes; median tail latency increased 3x on affected nodes.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1), Redwood Hosted; tenant pinned to dedicated GPU pool with soft autoscaling.
- Traffic pattern: large batch initialization + concurrent real-time queries.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Simulated morning ramp: a short surge of ~4–6x baseline concurrent session initializations with long-poll generation calls.
2) Inflight queue depth per-tenant reached configured limit (default 128) on several serving workers.
3) Serving runtime started applying backpressure; streaming proxy began returning partial frames then silence; client SDKs saw TCP keepalive without new SSE messages.
4) Autoscaler attempted to add capacity but hit scale-up cooldown and scheduling delay due to quota for ephemeral GPUs.

Logs / evidence:
- Support traces: trace IDs provided by customer: [trace: c3f9a1b2, c3f9a1c8, c3f9a2f0] (see attached logs in support ticketing UI).
- Grafana dashboards: tenant_inflight_queue_depth (spike to 128), worker_streaming_frame_errors (jump), node_gpu_utilization (70%->95% on 4 nodes).
- Slack: #support thread #incidents/voltline-3-8 contains live notes and customer screenshots.

Immediate customer-facing actions taken:
- Engaged SRE and Escalation SEs; provided Voltline a status update and temporary mitigation guidance.
- Applied per-tenant temporary increase of inflight queue_soft_limit to 256 for Voltline while we investigate (mitigation window started 2026-03-08T09:05Z).
- Issued partial credit offer while we complete RCA; billing team looped in.

Current hypothesis and scope:
- Primary hypothesis: combination of large-batch session warmups plus many long-running generation requests filled per-tenant inflight queue slots and caused the streaming proxy to drop frames rather than queue them for KV/cache reuse.
- Secondary hypothesis: autoscaler cooldown and a scheduling bottleneck (burst quota) prevented rapid capacity add, amplifying the customer impact.

2026-03-08 09:45 - Marta Ruiz (CS): Applied temporary inflight queue soft limit increase for Voltline and confirmed streaming recovery for most sessions. Customer requests a permanent remediation plan.

2026-03-10 08:55 - Voltline (Customer): Accepted temporary credits; requested clear ETA for fix and asks for prevention steps during future campaigns.
investigation_notes: Confirmed pattern correlates with tenant_inflight_queue_depth. Affected nodes exhibited elevated GC pauses (~150–220ms) on runtime thread pools coincident with long-generation tails.
Heap and GC profiling on r-srv-15 shows increased allocation rate from session state capture on large-batch inits; memory churn may have contributed to short stalls causing backlog growth.

Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts: two scale-outs initiated at 08:33 and 08:40, second one failed due to ephemeral GPU quota limit. Ticket INT-4421 opened to lift ephemeral quota for the pool.

SDK behavior: v1.4.2 reuses SSE connection but has 3s keepalive threshold which delays detection of silent streams; customer on v1.4.2 may see longer outage window. Recommend SDK upgrade v1.5.0 which includes improved keepalive and exponential reconnect.
Related signals: increased worker_streaming_frame_errors and client-side reconnects. No authorization or PII leaks detected in transcripts checked so far.

Reproduced in staging using a synthetic morning-ramp job that spawns 600 concurrent sessions with mixed short and long-generation calls; observed same inflight queue saturation and frame dropping in staging worker set.
root_cause: Per-tenant inflight queue reached hard soft-limit during a synchronized customer batch ramp. The streaming proxy lacked buffering fallback and dropped frames when backend latency increased; autoscaler response was delayed due to ephemeral GPU quota and scale cooldown, amplifying the outage window.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: increased per-tenant inflight soft limit for Voltline to 256 (temporary) and advised Voltline to stagger large batch initializations. Observed immediate decrease in streaming silence incidents.

Mid-term fix implemented: merged github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342 which adds bounded buffering in the streaming-proxy, emits metrics for frame-drop events, and fails open to preserve partial streaming rather than silent TCP holds. Deployed to us-east-1 canary 2026-03-10 02:00Z.

Autoscaler change: lowered scale cooldown window for dedicated pools from 5m to 90s for burst scenarios and added preemptive scale policy targeting queue-depth threshold. Config change deployed 2026-03-10 04:30Z.
Customer communication: provided Voltline with timeline, temporary credit offer, and suggested SDK upgrade path; scheduled follow-up call for 2026-03-12 to review long-term mitigation.
No customer data exposure detected; security engaged for audit verification.
follow_up_actions: 1) (Ownership: Runtime) Add unit/integration test covering inflight queue saturation -> ensure streaming-proxy bounded buffering preserves SSE frames where possible. ETA: 2026-03-24.
2) (Ownership: Autoscaler) Implement alert on tenant_inflight_queue_depth > 75% sustained for 2m with an automated preemptive scale. ETA: 2026-03-17.

3) (Ownership: Customer Success) Run postmortem call with Voltline on 2026-03-12; document operational guidelines for large batch campaigns and SDK upgrade instructions. Owner: Marta Ruiz. ETA: 2026-03-12.
4) (Ownership: Billing) Apply one-time service credit for impacted window and confirm in ticket. Owner: Alex Chen. ETA: 2026-03-13.
5) (Ownership: Infra) Review ephemeral GPU quota for dedicated pools; propose quota increase or burst reservation for enterprise tenants. Report by 2026-03-18.
